newsitem.title: USA: Olympics Committee, World Bank to work together. [CORRECTED 02:30 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Olympics Committee, World Bank to work together. [CORRECTED 02:30 GMT]

text.p: In an unusual merger of muscle with money, the International Olympic Committee and the World Bank said on Thursday they would work together to promote sustainable human development worldwide.

An agreement signed by International Olympic Committee (IOC) President Juan Antonio Samaranch and World Bank President James Wolfensohn called for creation of a joint working group to develop a programme of cooperation.
Possibilities included distribution of soccer balls in poor neighbourhoods, development of playing fields at World Bank construction projects and nutrition advice to athletes.

"Personally it means a great deal to me," said Wolfensohn, who competed at the 1956 Olympics as an Australian fencer (corrects from "who won a silver medal in fencing at the 1956 Olympics"). "I know the ideals of the Olympic movement and I see how congruous they are with the work of the World Bank."
Added Samaranch: "We are convinced that our cooperation in field projects in favour of developing countries will be very positive."

The World Bank is an intergovenmental agency with 180 member countries that lends tens of billions of dollars each year to developing nations. The IOC is a non-profit, non-governmental organisation for 197 member national Olympic committees that conduct athletic programmes in their countries.
